q2: SELECT t2.c1 AS beer, MIN(t5.c3) AS price, t5.c1 AS bar FROM t2 LEFT JOIN t5 ON t2.c1 = t5.c2 GROUP BY t2.c1, t5.c1 HAVING COUNT(t5.c1) > 0 ORDER BY t2.c1;
explanation: Q1 computes, for each beer (t5.c2), the overall minimum price (MIN(t5.c3)) and then returns only those offer rows (via an inner equality join on both beer and price) that match that minimum price. In contrast, Q2 groups t5 by beer and bar so that it returns a row for every bar offering the beer, regardless of whether the bar’s price is the overall minimum; it just reports the single price that bar offers. Thus, if a beer is offered at multiple prices—with one bar offering the minimum and another offering a higher price—Q1 returns only the minimal-price row while Q2 returns rows for both bars.
